newsitem.title: GERMANY: Some winter crops damaged in eastern Germany.
newsitem.headline: Some winter crops damaged in eastern Germany.

text.p: German winter barley, rape and wheat crops in eastern Germany suffered some damage from frost and snow earlier this month, the DWD meteorological office said on Thursday.
"Damage is now becoming evident in the areas with insufficient snow cover," a DWD source said.
"We've heard of winter kill in Brandenburg state around Berlin...it's far from the disastrous conditions seen last year but it's not unproblematic."

Geographically more exposed to harsh winter weather, former eastern Germany suffered severe damage in 1995/96. Grain crop yields last year were on average 10 percent lower than the year before and the rapeseed crop was nearly halved.

Conditions in the West were better and were expected to remain stable across the country as a new cold front was forecast for the next seven days, bringing temperatures to between two degrees and minus two degrees C during the day, DWD said.
That is no longer dangerous for dormant winter crops.
A farm union statement from the key agricultural region of Lower Saxony in the northwest said rapeseed and grain crops were developing well after the first wave of frost attacks.
Marginal damage should be overcome when plants recovered in the spring.
But there was a chance of more frost in February and plants had not received enough rain in the winter months.
